question: The Narmada River originates from which hills?
solution:
The Correct answer is __**Satpura Hills**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Narmada River** originates from the **Amarkantak Plateau**, which is located in the **Satpura Hills** of Madhya Pradesh, India.
 
• The Narmada is the **fifth-largest river in India** and the **largest west-flowing river** in the country.
 
• It flows through the states of **Madhya Pradesh**, **Maharashtra**, and **Gujarat** before emptying into the **Arabian Sea**.
 
• The river is often referred to as the **"Lifeline of Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat"** due to its significance in providing water for agriculture, drinking, and electricity generation.
 
• It is also known for its **cultural and religious significance**, with many temples and ghats located along its banks.
 
• One of the prominent landmarks on the river is the **Sardar Sarovar Dam**, which is a multipurpose project aimed at irrigation, hydropower, and water supply.
 
• The **Narmada Valley** is rich in biodiversity and is home to a variety of flora and fauna, some of which are endemic to the region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Western Ghats**__

 __
 
• The **Western Ghats** are a mountain range that runs parallel to the western coast of India.
 
• They are known for their **rich biodiversity** and have been declared a **UNESCO World Heritage Site**.
 
• Some major rivers originating from the Western Ghats include the **Godavari, Krishna, and Kaveri**.
 
 
 
• **Vindhyachal**__
 __
 
• The **Vindhyachal range** is a mountain range in central India, separating the northern and southern parts of the country.
 
• It is not the origin of the Narmada River but plays a significant role in Indian geography by forming a natural boundary.
 
 
 
• **Aravalli**__
 
 
• The **Aravalli Hills** are one of the oldest mountain ranges in the world, located in western India.
 
• The range extends across **Rajasthan, Haryana, and Gujarat**.
 
• It is not related to the origin of the Narmada River but is known for its **mineral deposits** and ecological significance.
